title: Tip: inspect the query before you run it
message: After a search, open Query preview to see the Wikimedia request assembled from your active filters. It is a quick way to spot an over-specific combination.

title: Tip: your search is a shareable recipe
message: Search terms, filters, sort order, location, and even Grid or Map view are encoded in the URL. Copy it to share the recipe—not a frozen result list.

title: Tip: Map and Grid share one search
message: Switching to Map keeps the current query and loaded results. Use Map to discover a nearby point, then return to Grid without rebuilding your search.

title: Tip: Browse is for finding Commons vocabulary
message: When ordinary words are not finding the right files, Browse Categories, Templates, or Depicts subjects and apply a result back into Search.

title: Tip: long-press a card to select files
message: Long-press a media card to enter selection mode, then add files to the persistent download queue as you browse different views.

title: Tip: selecting a file does not download it
message: The download queue stores public file references only. Media bytes are fetched when you explicitly start a verified ZIP job or an individual download.

title: Tip: open viewer sections when you need them
message: Structured data, related media, and global usage load when expanded. You can inspect the core file details first without requesting every optional panel.

title: Tip: start attribution from the viewer
message: The How to use this file panel can produce plain text, HTML, or WikiText attribution from the file metadata. Always compare it with the original Commons page before publishing.

title: Tip: follow an uploader into a portfolio
message: Found one useful file? Open its uploader portfolio to explore that Wikimedia username's other uploads without guessing new search terms.

title: Tip: start pipelines with three nodes
message: Try Text Query → Format Filter → Dataset Manifest. Run a preview before exporting, then grow the graph once the simple workflow makes sense.

title: Tip: pipelines can combine branches
message: Use set operations to union, intersect, or subtract two media branches. This is useful when one search describes the subject and another describes the constraint.

title: Tip: check the request log when something feels odd
message: The receipt icon in the top-right of the landing page shows the Wikimedia requests CommonsLens made and the status each one returned.

title: Tip: use + to search separate ideas
message: Write `mozart + beethoven` with spaces around the plus sign to run two independent searches, merge their results, and remove duplicate files. It is OR-style branching, not a requirement that one file contain both terms.

title: Tip: exclude a term with -word
message: Use `red fox -dog` to remove results containing dog. Keep the minus sign attached to the term; use `-"domestic dog"` when the exclusion is an exact phrase.

title: Tip: quote an exact phrase
message: Use quotation marks around a phrase such as `"red fox"` when word order matters. Quotes make a stricter phrase search; they are not a general make-this-term-mandatory switch.

title: Tip: search only file titles
message: Try `intitle:"Eiffel Tower"` when the phrase must occur in the Commons file or page title instead of anywhere in indexed text.

title: Tip: limit a query with filetype:
message: Native operators such as `filetype:video`, `filetype:audio`, `filetype:bitmap`, and `filetype:office` can narrow a text query. The media tabs are often easier when you do not need to type the operator.

title: Tip: search a known category directly
message: Use `incategory:"Architecture"` for files directly in a named Commons category. Use the Categories filter when you need the app’s nested-subcategory control.

title: Tip: find pages using a template
message: Use `hastemplate:"Quality image"` or another template name to search file pages carrying that template. A template is page metadata, not the same thing as a category.

title: Tip: search Structured Data with a Q-code
message: A query such as `haswbstatement:P180=Q146` searches a Wikidata statement—in this example, files whose Structured Data says they depict a cat. Use Depicts or property filters when you want autocomplete.

title: Tip: search raw description-page text
message: Use `insource:"{{Information"` to look for literal text in file-page source. This searches wikitext rather than the normal title, description, and category index.

title: Tip: use insource regex sparingly
message: Slash-delimited patterns such as `insource:/monument.*historique/` can find flexible wikitext matches, but regular expressions can be expensive. Start with literal text when possible.

title: Tip: complete a word with a wildcard
message: `cat*` matches words beginning with cat and continuing with zero or more characters. The wildcard cannot begin a word, so use it as a suffix rather than `*cat`.

title: Tip: try fuzzy or proximity matching
message: Add `~` after a word for approximate spelling, or use a distance such as `"red fox"~2` when the words may appear close together rather than as one exact phrase.

title: Tip: know the difference between OR and +
message: `cat OR dog` is native CirrusSearch boolean syntax. CommonsLens `cat + dog` is different: it runs independent branches and merges them, which is useful when ordinary boolean grouping would be unclear.

title: Tip: autocomplete is not the full search
message: Selecting an autocomplete suggestion opens a direct file-title search. Press Enter instead when you want Wikimedia to search the whole phrase you typed.

title: Tip: multiple format chips mean any selected format
message: Selecting PNG and SVG asks for either format; it does not require one file to be both. Use the media tab as well when you want to limit the broader media family.

title: Tip: remove one active filter from its chip
message: Active filters appear as removable chips in the search workspace. Delete the last chip that changed the result set before rebuilding the whole search from scratch.

title: Tip: switch between Intersection and Union
message: Use Intersection when one file must satisfy every included subject, category, property, or template. Use Union when any included value is enough; exclusions remain exclusions either way.

title: Tip: nested categories can become very broad
message: Include nested subcategories uses Commons’ deep-category search and can time out on a broad root. Turn it off or choose narrower categories when results are incomplete or unexpectedly empty.

title: Tip: original dates come from file metadata
message: Originally made / photographed uses available fields such as DateTimeOriginal, not the upload or page-edit date. Files without a parseable original date cannot satisfy that range.

title: Tip: attribution filtering may happen after search
message: Attribution required is based on metadata returned for each file rather than a single CirrusSearch keyword. A broad query may need additional result pages before the requested set is filled.

title: Tip: Quality and above is a convenience tier
message: The Quality filter’s “this tier + above” option groups named Commons assessments in the displayed order. It is a discovery shortcut, not an official numeric quality score.

title: Tip: you can start with filters only
message: You do not need a text phrase first. Choose a media scope, format, license, location, or technical filter to discover files by a requirement rather than a word.

title: Tip: date fields use an open-ended range
message: Enter only From for on-or-after, only Before for earlier-than, or both for a bounded range. The date field matters: submitted, edited, and original dates describe different events.

title: Tip: coordinate and nearby-title searches are alternatives
message: A point-and-radius location search clears a competing nearby-title location. If the result set looks geographically wrong, check which location chip is active before adding more filters.

title: Tip: directory counts are vocabulary clues
message: Category, template, and subject directories show names and counts to help you choose Commons terminology. A count is a discovery signal, not a guarantee that every item will load into the next search.

title: Tip: apply a directory result back to Search
message: Select a category, template, or depicted subject in Browse, then use its search action to carry the exact value into the main Search workspace instead of retyping it.

title: Tip: templates and categories answer different questions
message: A category organizes files by topic or collection; a template is metadata attached to a file page. Browse both when an institution, source, or rights workflow is difficult to find with ordinary words.

title: Tip: choose the exact Depicts entity
message: When Browse or autocomplete offers several labels, choose the Wikidata entity you mean. The stored Q-code is more reliable than relying on a spelling that can refer to several people or places.

title: Tip: broad directory roots are not always practical
message: Deep category searches can exceed Commons’ category limits. Narrow the directory term, disable nested mode, or search separate categories when a large root becomes slow.

title: Tip: use Browse to learn the words, then Search to combine them
message: Browse is strongest when you do not know the exact Commons label. Once you find the right category or template, combine it with text, formats, dates, or rights in Search.

title: Tip: nearby map searches have a 500 m floor
message: The map clamps a nearby-search radius to at least 0.5 km, or 500 metres. A smaller value is raised to 500 m, so use the result metadata and map context when you need a tighter visual inspection.

title: Tip: tapping the map changes the actual search
message: A map tap is not just a pin. It becomes the center of a new nearby-media search, updates the Search state, and carries the location back to Grid.

title: Tip: panning does not change the location filter
message: Panning, zooming, and rotating only change the camera. Tap a new point and apply the radius when you want to search a different place.

title: Tip: open a cluster before choosing a file
message: Numbered markers represent several loaded results at the current zoom. Select a cluster to open its file sheet, then choose a file or zoom in for individual markers.

title: Tip: not every result can become a marker
message: Map plots only loaded results with usable coordinates. A file can remain in the result preview without a marker because it has no mappable location metadata.

title: Tip: load more results to reveal more markers
message: Map only knows about the Search results loaded so far. Use Load more or continue scrolling the result preview when the mapped count is smaller than the collection you are exploring.

title: Tip: open map attribution when you need provider terms
message: The layer control cycles through street, satellite, and hybrid presentations. Map attribution remains visible for the selected provider and its terms.

title: Tip: Map does not request your live device location
message: Map uses coordinates from the URL, filters, or the point you choose on the map. It does not ask for GPS permission or silently use your device location.

title: Tip: create a folder before collecting a theme
message: Open Bookmarks, choose Add folder, and name an album before you start sorting. You can also create a folder from a card’s folder picker while assigning one file.

title: Tip: one bookmark can belong to several folders
message: Folder membership is separate from the main bookmark collection. Put a file in multiple folders for overlapping projects without duplicating the saved URL.

title: Tip: removing a folder is not deleting its files
message: Remove a file from one folder to change only that album. Removing the bookmark itself removes it from All Bookmarked Media and every folder.

title: Tip: bookmarks are references, not snapshots
message: CommonsLens stores the public file URL and reloads current Wikimedia metadata when you open Bookmarks. Recheck the source page before relying on old rights or attribution details.

title: Tip: search bookmarks by uploader and categories too
message: The Bookmarks search field can match loaded title, URL, description, object name, uploader, and category text—not just the visible filename.

title: Tip: bulk-assign bookmarked files to folders
message: Use Select media to add to a folder from All Bookmarked Media, choose several cards, and add the selection to one or more folders at once.

title: Tip: a shared bookmarks URL does not share your folders
message: A bookmarks link can preserve the page, search text, and selected folder identifier, but another browser does not receive your local bookmark URLs or folder contents.

title: Tip: portfolio order is upload order
message: An author portfolio starts with the uploader’s newest uploads. Newest does not mean the photograph, scan, recording, or depicted event was created most recently.

title: Tip: uploader and creator can be different people
message: A portfolio is keyed to a Wikimedia account. Inspect each file’s creator, source, institution, and license separately before treating the account as the author of the work.

title: Tip: a + after the portfolio count means more pages
message: The portfolio count describes items currently loaded. Scroll toward the end to request older uploads while the count still shows a trailing plus.

title: Tip: use the arrow keys in the viewer
message: When a file comes from a result queue, Left and Right arrow keys move through neighboring results on desktop. The header shows the current position, such as 3 OF 50.

title: Tip: direct file links have no surrounding queue
message: Opening a viewer URL with only a file identifier shows DIRECT LINK. Add a search, portfolio, bookmarks, map, or pipeline context when you want surrounding navigation.

title: Tip: WEB and FULL change the preview, not the license
message: For images and vectors, WEB is lighter and FULL is larger when available. The choice affects the displayed URL and is remembered locally; it does not change metadata or reuse terms.

title: Tip: related media is another discovery path
message: Expand Related Media in the viewer to follow Wikimedia’s similarity results. Use it to explore neighboring files, then verify each file independently.

title: Tip: an empty Structured Data panel is still information
message: No statements means CommonsLens did not receive structured claims to display for that file. It does not prove that the file has no description, license, or useful metadata elsewhere.

title: Tip: the queue deduplicates and stops at 500 entries
message: Selecting the same canonical media URL from different views reuses one queue item. The browser-local queue accepts up to 500 entries, so split very large collections into deliberate batches.

title: Tip: Export CSV does not fetch media bytes
message: CSV export creates a metadata manifest with Wikimedia URLs. Choose Download Original or Download ZIP when you actually need the image, audio, video, or document bytes.

title: Tip: large ZIP jobs arrive as numbered parts
message: CommonsLens rotates ZIP output by entry count and byte budget so a large selection does not require one enormous browser Blob. Check the browser downloads panel for every part.

title: Tip: download validation is not rights clearance
message: A file can pass transport, type, size, and integrity checks and still require attribution or have other reuse restrictions. Verify the original Commons source page before publishing.

title: Tip: the browser controls multi-download permission
message: A ZIP job or several explicit downloads may trigger the browser’s multiple-download permission. CommonsLens cannot choose your download folder or recall files already handed to the browser.

title: Tip: a pipeline needs a Dataset Manifest sink
message: A graph is not runnable until a Dataset Manifest (CSV) node finishes the branch. Legacy output nodes may still be readable in old graphs but are not the current palette workflow.

title: Tip: Preview 100 records before a full export
message: Preview is capped for quick logic checks. Run full export when you need continuation pages and a complete metadata CSV; preview is not proof that a large dataset is exhausted.

title: Tip: Combine Constraints and Intersect are different
message: Use Combine Constraints (AND) while both branches are query-capable and should become one server-side search. Use Intersect after two branches are already materialized and must be compared by media URL.

title: Tip: Field Select changes export columns, not thumbnails
message: Field Select projects the records used for output. It does not remove the underlying media item from the preview or transform the file itself.

title: Tip: put Sample / Limit before Enrich
message: Enrich can make extra metadata requests for every incoming item. Put Sample / Limit before it when you want a smaller test run, then enable only the metadata bundles you need.

title: Tip: pipeline edits autosave in this browser
message: Node positions, connections, settings, titles, and notes are saved locally as you edit. Rename the graph so it is recognizable in Saved pipelines.

title: Tip: pipeline JSON is a recipe, not a result backup
message: Export as JSON carries the graph definition, not fetched media, query caches, or a completed CSV. Import it elsewhere, review its usernames and coordinates, then run it there.

title: Tip: clear pipeline cache without deleting the graph
message: The pipeline Clear Cache action removes locally cached query and enrichment results while preserving the saved graph. Use it when you need fresh requests or more browser storage space.

title: Tip: a shared URL is a recipe, not a frozen result list
message: Search URLs preserve query text, filters, sort, location, and Map/Grid presentation. The recipient runs a new request, so result order, metadata, and availability can differ later.

title: Tip: local bookmarks and pipelines do not travel with a URL
message: URLs can restore a view or recipe, but browser-local bookmarks, folders, saved graphs, caches, queues, and viewer preferences need their own export or recreation on another device.

title: Tip: treat query URLs as visible data
message: Search terms, usernames, categories, coordinates, and filter choices can appear in browser history, messages, screenshots, and logs. Do not put confidential research terms or sensitive locations in a shared URL.
